title: Framed tensor twists of the symmetric algebra
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $n\in\mathbb N$. Put $\mathcal E_n=\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, with $\mathcal L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\mathcal E_n$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type. Give $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E_n)$ their symmetric-degree gradings and canonical degree-one inclusions $j$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra; lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded].
For every open $U\subseteq S$ and frame $e\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal L)$ (meaning $a\mapsto ae$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal L|_U$), the map $\tau_e:v\mapsto v\otimes e^{\otimes n}$ is a module isomorphism $\mathcal E|_U\to\mathcal E_n|_U$, with inverse $v\otimes ae^{\otimes n}\mapsto av$. There is a unique graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebra isomorphism $\beta_e:\mathcal A|_U\to\mathcal B|_U$ fixing scalars and satisfying $\beta_e(j(v))=j(v\otimes e^{\otimes n})$. Its inverse extends $\tau_e^{-1}$. On each affine $V\subseteq U$, the canonical affine-section identifications identify $\beta_e(V)$ with the symmetric-algebra map of $\tau_e(V)$, and the maps in both directions commute with restriction to every smaller open subset. Under the canonical restriction identifications, $\beta_e|_V=\beta_{e|_V}$.
If $u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)^\times$ and $e'=ue$, then $\tau_{e'}=u^n\tau_e$ and, for every $k\geq0$ and every local homogeneous section $a\in\mathcal A_k$, one has $\beta_{e'}(a)=u^{nk}\beta_e(a)$. For $n=0$, the maps $\tau_e$ and $\beta_e$ are the canonical unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 02NC, label lemma-twisting-and-proj, proof: trivialize the invertible module and glue; symmetric-algebra specialization

proof.text: First fix the restriction identifications. For an open $U$, the inclusion of the site of opens contained in $U$ into the site of opens of $S$ is continuous and cocontinuous: a cover of any $W\subseteq U$ is the very same family on both sites. Both sites are small (their objects are sets of opens). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction] identifies restriction of a sheafification with sheafification of the restricted presheaf, preserving its unit sections. Apply this to the tensor presheaf [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and to the symmetric-algebra presheaf [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. This gives $(F\otimes G)|_U=F|_U\otimes G|_U$ and $\operatorname{Sym}(F)|_U=\operatorname{Sym}(F|_U)$. The latter identification preserves scalars, generators and multiplication: on original presheaf sections these are the identical operations, and the comparison's hom-ext clause verifies the multiplication equality one linear variable at a time. The item's $\operatorname{Sym}(F)$ with $j_F$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] is identified with this explicit sheafification by the unique algebra maps in both directions preserving the degree-one maps: the explicit model has the same universal property by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core], so both composites fix $j_F$ and are identities by uniqueness; the same holds over $U$. These are the canonical identifications used below.

source.place: Tag 04B8, label lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification; module slice application Tag 04IY, sites-modules-lemma-relocalize

proof.text: Fix a frame $e$ over $U$ and write $c:\mathcal L|_U\to\mathcal O_U$ for its inverse, so $c(ae)=a$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. The balanced map $(v,ae)\mapsto av$ gives an inverse to $v\mapsto v\otimes e$: on pure tensors the composites are $v\mapsto v$ and $v\otimes ae\mapsto av\otimes e=v\otimes ae$. These formulas commute with restrictions. They therefore descend through the sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; the same uniqueness checks the composite identities after sheafification. Induct on $m$: start with the identity frame of $\mathcal L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_U$, and repeat this tensor calculation with $e$ to obtain the frame $e^{\otimes(m+1)}$ from $e^{\otimes m}$. Applying the identical calculation to $\mathcal E|_U$ and the resulting frame of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}|_U$ gives $\tau_e$ and its asserted inverse. No tensor-section comparison on a nonaffine open is assumed.

source.place: Section Tag 03EK, label section-tensor-product, presheaf tensor and sheafification formulas; Tag 03CY, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: Frames cover $S$ by [def-sc-invertible-module]. On each framed open the previous step identifies $\mathcal E_n$ with $\mathcal E$. Let $x\in S$ and let $W\ni x$ be a framed open with frame $e$. Restriction of quasi-coherent modules to an open is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], so $\mathcal E|_W$ is quasi-coherent; by the definition [pqf-def-coherent] applied on the scheme $W$, $x$ has an affine neighbourhood $V\subseteq W$ (affine opens of $W$ are affine opens of $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]) with $\mathcal E|_V\cong\widetilde M$. Composing with $\tau_e|_V$ gives $\mathcal E_n|_V\cong\widetilde M$. For finite type choose a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ and a surjection $\mathcal O_N^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal E|_N$; its restriction to $N\cap W$ is still surjective (surjectivity of sheaf maps is local) and composing with $\tau_e$ gives a surjection onto $\mathcal E_n|_{N\cap W}$. This proves both required properties of $\mathcal E_n$ [pqf-def-coherent]. The same restriction lemma makes $\mathcal E|_U$ and $\mathcal E_n|_U$ quasi-coherent, so the symmetric-algebra universal property may now be applied over $U$.

source.place: Tag 02NC, label lemma-twisting-and-proj, proof: choose an open covering trivializing the invertible sheaf; finite type and quasi-coherence transported locally

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] on the scheme $U$ to the linear map $j_{\mathcal E_n}\tau_e$ and, in the other direction, to $j_{\mathcal E}\tau_e^{-1}$. It gives algebra maps $b$ and $b'$ fixing scalars. Their composites send every generator $j(v)$ to itself, since $\tau_e^{-1}\tau_e=1$ and $\tau_e\tau_e^{-1}=1$. Uniqueness in that same universal property makes the composites identities and makes $b$ the unique algebra map with the stated normalization. Set $\beta_e=b$ under step 1's restriction identifications. For an affine $V\subseteq U$, the affine comparison in the cited node identifies $b(V)$ with the unique ring-level symmetric-algebra map extending $\tau_e(V)$: both maps agree on degree-one generators, so [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] makes them equal. The identical argument applies to $b'(V)$.

source.place: Section Tag 01CF, label section-symmetric-exterior; canonical affine comparison of Schemes Section Tag 01LA, item (9)

proof.text: On an affine open $V\subseteq U$, a degree-$k$ symmetric element is a sum of scalar multiples of products $j(v_1)\cdots j(v_k)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], using the affine comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. The generator formula in step 4 sends each such product to $j(\tau_e v_1)\cdots j(\tau_e v_k)$, again in degree $k$. The inverse has the same property. Use the canonical affine-basis graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]: its degree components are precisely these submodules, its restrictions preserve them, and its rings identify with the affine sections of the sheaf. The calculation therefore proves degree preservation on every member of the affine basis; for an arbitrary local homogeneous section restrict to an affine cover inside its domain [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The images belong to the same degree on that cover, hence belong to the corresponding degree subsheaf on the original open by its sheaf condition. Hence $\beta_e$ is graded; its uniqueness among graded algebra isomorphisms follows from its already established uniqueness among algebra maps.

source.place: Section Tag 01CF, label section-symmetric-exterior, graded quotient construction; Tag 01CG, label lemma-local-tensor-algebra, symmetric-degree sheafification

proof.text: The tensor formulas of step 2 commute with all restrictions, for $e$, $e^{\otimes n}$ and the inverse coefficient map $c$. Moreover $b$ and $b'$ are morphisms of algebra sheaves by step 4 [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra], so for every smaller open $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ and section $a$ one has $b(a)|_W=b(a|_W)$, and likewise for $b'$. To check the stronger normalization $\beta_e|_V=\beta_{e|_V}$ even when $V$ is nonaffine, use the canonical restriction identification from step 1 [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction]. Both maps fix scalars and send $j(v)$ to $j(v\otimes(e|_V)^{\otimes n})$. The sheaf universal property's uniqueness over the scheme $V$ identifies them. This also proves the claimed restriction compatibility under the affine-section identifications of step 4.

source.place: Section Tag 01CF, label section-symmetric-exterior; restriction comparison Tag 04B8, sites-lemma-almost-cocontinuous-sheafification

proof.text: Let $e'=ue$. Tensor balancing gives $(ue)^{\otimes n}=u^n e^{\otimes n}$ by induction on $n$, with base $1=u^0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; hence $\tau_{e'}=u^n\tau_e$. The unit hypothesis ensures $ue$ is a frame, since its coefficient inverse is $u^{-1}c$. On a product of $k$ generators the normalization of step 4 now gives $\beta_{e'}(j(v_1)\cdots j(v_k))=(u^n)^k\beta_e(j(v_1)\cdots j(v_k))=u^{nk}\beta_e(j(v_1)\cdots j(v_k))$. Scalar linearity extends this to the whole degree-$k$ component on each affine open by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] and the affine comparison [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. For a local homogeneous section restrict to an affine cover [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], apply this equality, and use uniqueness of sections of a sheaf to obtain it on the original open. When $k=0$ this is the scalar identity. When $n=0$, step 2 is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$ with inverse $v\otimes a\mapsto av$; uniqueness of the symmetric-algebra extension makes $\beta_e$ the induced canonical unit identification, independent of $e$.
